description: Wire per-branch pricing into the POS sale flow (gap-analysis Section 5A item 1 + item 2 + free item 5). Unify branch ids to b1/b2/b3, add a shared pure price-resolution helper that resolves by product CODE scaled by UOM ratio, call it at the add-to-cart boundary in both POS screens, switch POSSaleScreen to productStore, and prove it with a vitest. This is the biggest gap and must land first; independent of FEAT-002 and FEAT-003.
steps: Unify branch ids (plan Decision A): in src/store/pricingStore.ts MOCK_DOCS change branchId 'branch-01' -> 'b1' (branchName 'สาขาหลัก') and 'branch-02' -> 'b2' (branchName 'สาขา 1'); in src/data/mockBranches.ts retarget MOCK_BRANCHES ids to b1/b2/b3 with names สาขาหลัก / สาขา 1 / สาขา เชียงใหม่ (matching useUserBranches.ALL_BRANCHES). Do NOT modify useUserBranches.ALL_BRANCHES or branchPermissionStore default.

Create a shared pure helper src/utils/priceResolver.ts exporting resolveCartPrice(master: ProductMaster, uom: ProductUOM, branchId?: string): { price: number; source: 'branch' | 'central' | 'base' }. It calls usePricingStore.getState().resolvePrice(master.code, branchId) (plan Decision B: pass master.code, NOT master.id). On hit: price = round2(resolved.price * uom.ratio) with source = resolved.sourceType; on miss: price = uom.salePrice, source = 'base' (plan Decision C). No React imports; add a comment explaining branch price = base-unit price scaled by ratio.

In src/screens/web/WebPOSScreen.tsx: read activeBranchId via useBranchGuard(); route the price in toCartProduct (or its call sites building cart Products) through resolveCartPrice(master, uom, activeBranchId). Keep existing masterProducts/ALL_BASE/handleProductTap/barcode flow working. Optionally show the active branch name in the POS header.

In src/screens/sale/POSSaleScreen.tsx: source products from useProductStore().products instead of static MOCK_PRODUCTS/ALL_CART_PRODUCTS (mirror WebPOSScreen's reactive masterProducts pattern), and apply resolveCartPrice using activeBranchId from useBranchGuard() at the toCartProduct boundary. Keep UOM selector + barcode scan working (findProductByBarcode may still take the current product list).

Add vitest src/utils/__tests__/priceResolver.test.ts (style after src/engine/adapter/__tests__/cartAdapter.test.ts): with the b1 branch doc active, a base-UOM line for that product at b1 uses the branch newPrice; a non-base UOM scales by ratio; the same product at b3 (no branch doc) falls back to uom.salePrice; central doc applies when no branch doc exists. Inject/seed pricing docs deterministically so the test does not depend on today's date drift (docs use effective 2026-06 dates — set/override as needed).
Run tsc + tests; confirm no new tsc errors in touched files and no regression in cartAdapter (14) or engine (39/0).
acceptance_criteria: pricingStore MOCK_DOCS and mockBranches use branch ids b1/b2/b3 only; no 'branch-01'/'branch-02'/'branch-001' remain in those two files.
resolveCartPrice resolves by master.code and scales a hit by uom.ratio, falling back to uom.salePrice on miss.
Both WebPOSScreen and POSSaleScreen build cart line prices via resolveCartPrice with the active branch id; POSSaleScreen reads products from useProductStore.
`npm test` passes the new priceResolver suite AND still shows cartAdapter 14/14 + engine 39/0.
`npx tsc --noEmit` adds no new errors beyond the 13 baseline in any touched file.
verification: cd d:\pos-mobile\.worktrees\pricing-fix ; npx tsc --noEmit  (expect only the 13 pre-existing errors; none in pricingStore/mockBranches/priceResolver/WebPOSScreen/POSSaleScreen)
cd d:\pos-mobile\.worktrees\pricing-fix ; npm test  (expect new priceResolver suite pass; cartAdapter 14; engine self-test 39/0; 3 pre-existing load failures may remain)
findings: Canonical branch ids are b1/b2/b3 (names: b1='สาขาหลัก', b2='สาขา 1', b3='สาขา เชียงใหม่'), matching useUserBranches.ALL_BRANCHES and branchPermissionStore default (activeBranchId='b1'). pricingStore MOCK_DOCS now target b1 (prc-002 temp) and b2 (prc-003 perm); the central doc (prc-001) is unchanged. mockBranches.ts (incl. MOCK_ENTERPRISE_TERMINALS.branchId) retargeted to b1/b2/b3. Helper: src/utils/priceResolver.ts exports `resolveCartPrice(master: ProductMaster, uom: ProductUOM, branchId?: string): { price: number; source: 'branch'|'central'|'base' }` — pure, no React; calls usePricingStore.getState().resolvePrice(master.CODE, branchId) (key is CODE e.g. 'P001', NOT master.id 'p1'); on hit price=round2(resolved.price*uom.ratio) with source=resolved.sourceType; on miss price=uom.salePrice, source='base'. round2 = Math.round((n+EPSILON)*100)/100. Both POS screens resolve at the toCartProduct boundary and pass activeBranchId from useBranchGuard(); toCartProduct now takes an optional 3rd branchId arg. POSSaleScreen now sources products from useProductStore().products (reactive allCartProducts via useMemo over products+activeBranchId), removing static MOCK_PRODUCTS/ALL_CART_PRODUCTS; findProductByBarcode still receives the live `products` list. WebPOSScreen shows the active branch name on the cart header. TEST NOTE (reuse for later suites): any vitest importing a persisted store transitively imports persistStorage -> react-native + @react-native-async-storage/async-storage, which fail to resolve under happy-dom (the documented 'Libraries/Image/Image' load failure). priceResolver.test.ts works around this by mocking both at top: vi.mock('react-native', () => ({ Platform: { OS: 'web' } })) and vi.mock('@react-native-async-storage/async-storage', ...). It also seeds docs deterministically via usePricingStore.setState({documents:[...]}) with effectiveDate '2000-01-01' / expiryDate '2999-12-31' so results do not drift with today's date. RUNTIME-ONLY (unverified by build): switching the active branch to actually recompute POS prices depends on useBranchGuard reading branchStore (empty at runtime -> falls back to b1); verify on web that changing branch updates resolved prices. VERIFICATION: tsc --noEmit = exactly the 13 baseline errors, none in touched files; npm test = cartAdapter 14 + new priceResolver 5 (19 passing) + engine self-test 39/0; the 3 pre-existing suite-load failures remain.
